title: Tensor coordinates for smooth purity
statement: Use [def-pur-transport-canonical-pullback]. For a strong monoidal functor $F$ and $e:F(L)\simeq M$, define the comparison on nonnegative tensor powers recursively: the zeroth comparison is the inverse unit tensorator, and the successor comparison is the inverse binary tensorator followed by the previous comparison tensor $e$. The positive Tate lines are flat when $\ell$ is invertible on the scheme. Their product isomorphism is the recursion using the unitors and associators, with target the sum of the two exponents.

source.place: Coefficient, functor, counit and normalization clauses; coordinate interface TransportTensor

proof.text: The definitions powerPull and lineProduct remain their given unit/tensorator and unitor/associator recursions. For line_flat, invertibility of ell in every residue field implies invertibility in every stalk by the local residue map; the local unit criterion then gives IsUnit (ell : Gamma(X,top)). Apply [lem-poincare-integral-tate-local-basis] to the actual integral Tate module to obtain one pro-etale covering and regular-module identifications.

Prove flatness of the integral Tate module by descent. On the covering, the functors mapMod(u_i^*) jointly reflect isomorphisms: forget module actions, compare inverse image along the weakly etale u_i with localization restriction, and apply the source-library isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction, the pro-etale specialization of [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]. Forgetting module actions reflects isomorphisms. Each mapMod inverse image preserves finite limits and is strong monoidal. The local regular-module identifications make tensoring with its image left exact. Monoidal commTensorLeft identifies the composite of tensoring and inverse image with inverse image followed by local tensoring. For every finite diagram, jointlyReflectsLimit reflects the limiting mapped cone from these local composites. Thus tensoring with the integral Tate module is left exact. In a braided closed category this is flatness. This is the private proved flat_of_local_unit helper; it allows an empty covering of the empty scheme.

Apply [lem-sfb-internal-extension-preserves-flat] along coefficientMap (c.integralMap ell) X. This identifies the resulting flat object with c.firstLine ell X by its defining scalar extension, without a flatness assumption on the coefficient map. Induct on d: the regular tensor unit is flat at zero, and flat objects are closed under tensor products at successors. This proves line_flat for all six coefficient presentations, including zero finite coefficient rings.
